sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r3/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 6; Internal Quality Checks row 6, whose 'no network' wording is superseded by the skill's public-network delivery profile)

qc/runs/kittle-2026-10-09-r3/raw-evidence-index.json; qc/repairs/kittle-2026-10-08/results/golden-run.log (sha256 4da6ab5d... re-hashed, matches); qc/repairs/kittle-2026-10-08/tests/functional.cjs (sha256 b3b0ade7... re-hashed, matches); frozen solution/app/public/app.js and server.js re-hashed and match the index
evidence: Reachability: every capability the brief asks for is reachable from the seed and the pinned runtime. The agent image (environment/Dockerfile) is node:22-bookworm-slim with express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 installed globally and found via NODE_PATH, exactly as integration.md says; the verifier image pins the same packages (tests/Dockerfile:16-22), and test.sh:104-111 launches /app/server.js as uid 65534 under env -i with DB_PATH and PORT=3000, matching integration.md ('ordinary user', 'not necessarily from inside /app', DB_PATH honoured). The seed supplies every account, role, matter, wall (dev on M-12), timer, hold, earlier version, parent and read_up_to position the criteria rely on, and the fixed clock 2026-05-12T11:00:00Z is stated in integration.md and the seed. The boundary facts the criteria depend on are public: 'a message sent exactly seven days ago on a seven-day matter is already gone' (walls-and-retention.md:65) for K-10/K-11; 'When a hold is released, the timer applies straight away' (:71) for K-17; shortening deletes at once and turning off/lengthening never restores (:65) for K-13. Measured: the scripted golden run (qc/repairs/kittle-2026-10-08/results/golden-run.log, hashes verified and bound to the frozen solution files) reports PASS for all 16 functional criteria plus gate_constraints and polish_refusal_in_place, with a real process kill/restart and the app run as uid 65534 under env -i with cwd /tmp. That shows the brief is achievable in this environment; it is not a configured judge run, Oracle grade or model score. Single reading: the brief reads one way on every graded behaviour I traced (walls across list/thread/search/snippets/quotes/unread/mentions/links/transcripts; timers measured from sent time; holds per message; idempotent resend; same-time ordering by send order; nested replies with quotes; stale-edit refusal keeping typed text; literal markup everywhere; per-user unread synced across tabs; 390 px without sideways scroll; refusal reason that stays). Sign-out and account switching are not named but follow from 'sign in as different people' and the house identity convention (a known skill false positive). No step needs an off-machine address (app_context.md:26). Residual criterion-wording ambiguities a conforming app could fall on (none is an unreachable item and none changes the brief's main reading): (1) timer_changes step 2 (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:131) requires the replayed earlier-versions request to 'return not-available'. The brief says only that a gone message's earlier versions go with it (walls-and-retention.md:67); it prescribes a plain 'not available' for walled or foreign-matter requests (:59) and for link previews of gone messages (conversations.md:17), not for a versions request on a deleted message. An app returning 200 with an empty versions list leaks nothing but may be judged not 'not-available'. (2) 'A plain not-available answer' in signin_and_client_scope Part B (judge.toml:48) and wall_every_route step 3 (:61) can be read literally (that phrase) or semantically (a 404/'Not found' carrying no data); the brief quotes 'not available' (walls-and-retention.md:59), which favours the literal reading, so this is low risk but undefined for the judge. (3) polish transcript_print (tests/scored/polish/judge.toml) requires replies 'visibly set under' their parent so a thread can be followed 'without reading any "in reply to" text'; the brief only says the transcript lists messages 'oldest first in their threads' (walls-and-retention.md:77). A flat transcript with each reply directly after its parent and a 'Reply to ...' label is a second reasonable reading that fails this binary polish row. (4) deleted_and_expired_messages step 1 (judge.toml:112) says the reply shows 'a placeholder ... in place of a quote', while step 2 (:113) says it is 'shown under the same kind of deleted-message placeholder'; the brief accepts either ('above them we just want to see that the original message was deleted', walls-and-retention.md:67), so a judge could demand both forms. (5) Not a brief ambiguity but an unmeasured feasibility gap for alternatives: the copy-link legs (wall_mentions_and_links, message_links) say to copy the link with the app's control. The golden also shows the URL in a visible, selected text box (solution/app/public/app.js:443-451), but a conforming clipboard-only app needs the judge to read the clipboard in headless Playwright MCP, and app_context.md gives no method. No configured judge run shows this works. Weak-app probe: I found no brief gap that a broken app could exploit for this row. For example, a client-side-only wall is excluded by the explicit replay legs, and missing server idempotency is excluded by the exact-replay leg. Overall: there is no unreachable item, and the brief has one reasonable reading. The five items above are bounded P3 wording/feasibility risks. They are recorded for reconciliation, not waived. Configured judge, Oracle and model results are absent and are not claimed.
counterexample: Conforming app A answers the earlier-versions request for K-13 after the 7-day shortening with 200 {"versions":[]} (nothing leaks); a literal reading of timer_changes step 2 ('returns not-available') fails it. Conforming app B renders the transcript flat, oldest first, with each reply immediately after its parent and a 'Reply to Harriet: ...' label; it satisfies 'oldest first in their threads' (walls-and-retention.md:77) yet fails polish transcript_print. Conforming app C copies message links only to the clipboard; with no documented clipboard-read method the judge may report that it could not obtain the link and fail wall_mentions_and_links and message_links.
suggested_fix: In timer_changes step 2 accept 'not-available or an empty answer, with no 2,400 or 4,200'; define once in the functional prompt that 'not-available' means a refusal carrying no data, wording free; either add a brief sentence that transcript replies are indented under their parent or relax transcript_print to 'placed directly under and visibly grouped with'; let deleted_and_expired_messages accept either placeholder form; and add an app_context note on reading a copied link (visible link text, or grant clipboard-read in browser_run_code_unsafe and read navigator.clipboard).
